network.overall_strategy: No defended prebiotic experiment reaches free arginine, so the network prioritizes the two least-bad evidence-weighted families rather than disputed direct-arginine claims. The main family is Patel-style surface cyanosulfidic chemistry, which builds the C5 guanidino skeleton to the experimentally supported arginine alpha-aminonitrile through acrylonitrile, beta-aminopropionitrile, and Patel intermediates 35 and 37; hydrolysis to arginine is included but explicitly marked speculative. A second, weaker family treats ornithine as a late abiotic intermediate from HCN-rich chemistry and converts it to arginine by cyanamide guanidinylation, again flagged as unverified for the free amino acid. The citrulline/urea-cycle analogue and hydrothermal keto-acid routes are omitted as productive branches because the supplied literature offers only untested or purely thermodynamic support. The 10 pathways therefore combine four de novo cyanosulfidic routes, two ornithine endgames, and four shorter modular entry routes from advanced intermediates.

reactions.name: Photochemical cyanamide generation from HCN and ammonia

conditions.other: UV-irradiated HCN/NH3-rich surface waters; ammonium cyanide forms in situ; days to weeks

reactions.mechanism: Photochemical conversion of ammonium cyanide derived from HCN and NH3 into cyanamide, with urea and guanidine as likely coproduct classes.
reactions.reasoning: Lohrmann (1972) showed that irradiation of aqueous ammonium cyanide gives cyanamide together with urea and guanidine. This justifies treating cyanamide as an endogenous surface feedstock, although the chemistry is not selective and would operate as a mixed product pool rather than as a clean preparative step.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-mediated coupling of HCN and acetylene to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: UV-exposed cyanosulfidic streams or pools; localized copper-bearing settings required

reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-mediated hydrocyanation or cross-coupling of acetylene with HCN gives acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally placed acrylonitrile at the entry to the arginine branch using Cu(I) in a phosphate-buffered UV cyanosulfidic network. This is the best-supported C3 skeleton-forming step specific to the arginine-precursor branch in the supplied literature.

reactions.name: Acrylonitrile ammonolysis to beta-aminopropionitrile

conditions.other: Ammonia-rich near-neutral aqueous solution in phosphate-buffered surface settings

reactions.mechanism: Conjugate addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile forms the beta-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) identify beta-aminopropionitrile 34 from acrylonitrile plus ammonia as the common entry point for later arginine chemistry. This Michael-type addition is chemically straightforward and among the better grounded steps in the network.

reactions.name: HS-/UV reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation; HS-/H2S acts as stoichiometric photoreductant

reactions.mechanism: Sulfur-assisted photoreduction converts the nitrile to an aldehyde via reductive sulfur chemistry and hydrolytic workup.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) report H2S-driven photoreduction of beta-aminopropionitrile 34 to beta-aminopropionaldehyde 36, quoted in the review at 45% for this step. Because the chemistry depends on sulfidic photoredox, it inherits the locality and concentration constraints discussed by Ranjan et al. (2018).

reactions.name: Cyanamide guanidinylation of beta-aminopropionitrile

conditions.other: Concentrated cyanamide-bearing pool; near-neutral to mildly basic pH

reactions.mechanism: Addition of the terminal amine to cyanamide followed by proton transfers gives a guanidino-substituted nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) directly converted 34 with cyanamide to the guanidinylated nitrile 35, but explicitly described the reaction as relatively inefficient. It is nevertheless the main experimentally anchored route that installs the guanidino functionality before later chain extension.

reactions.name: Cyanamide addition to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: Cyanamide present together with the aldehyde intermediate in a surface flow system

reactions.mechanism: Reaction of the terminal amine with cyanamide gives a guanidinylated aminoaldehyde adduct, represented here as 3-guanidinopropanal.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) observed that residual cyanamide reacts very efficiently with beta-aminopropionaldehyde 36 to give adduct 37 and suggested this ordering helps feed the arginine-precursor branch. This aldehyde-first guanidinylation step is therefore better supported than free-ornithine guanidination, although the exact integrated flow sequence remains conditional in the paper.

reactions.name: Speculative reduction of guanidinylated beta-aminopropionitrile to the aldehyde analogue

conditions.other: UV irradiation; speculative ordering variant of the cyanosulfidic sequence

reactions.mechanism: Speculative sulfur-assisted photoreduction of the guanidinylated nitrile to the corresponding aldehyde, analogous to 34 to 36.
reactions.reasoning: No reaction in the supplied literature explicitly reports 35 converting to the aldehyde analogue of 37. This step is therefore speculative, but Patel et al. (2015) show the closely related 34 to 36 nitrile-to-aldehyde reduction and thus justify including a guanidinylate-first, reduce-later ordering as a chemically reasonable alternative branch.

reactions.name: Late cyanosulfidic homologation to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: UV-driven sequential flow chemistry through HCN homologation, thioamide and cyanohydrin stages, then Strecker addition

reactions.mechanism: HCN homologation and HS-/UV reduction convert the guanidinylated C3 aldehyde into a longer aldehyde-equivalent; subsequent Strecker chemistry with HCN and NH3 installs the alpha-aminonitrile to give arginine alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) tabulate the late sequence culminating in 46, the alpha-aminonitrile precursor of arginine, and frame integrated production conditionally rather than as a clean one-pot synthesis. This reaction compresses those documented late homologation and Strecker operations into a single network edge, and it therefore remains literature-guided but partly inferred; the required sulfidic setting is also environmentally local rather than globally guaranteed (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Speculative hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile to arginine

conditions.other: Mild hydrolytic conditions in pools or geothermal cycling; strong acid or base avoided because guanidino degradation is a concern

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration and hydrolysis convert the alpha-aminonitrile into the alpha-amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: This is the critical missing endgame: Patel et al. (2015) stop at the arginine alpha-aminonitrile and do not report free arginine. The review explicitly notes that no unambiguous prebiotic experiment has completed this hydrolysis, and older HCN-polymer hydrolysis assignments are confounded by non-reproducibility and side-product formation (Ferris et al., 1973; Ferris et al., 1974). This conversion is therefore necessary but explicitly speculative.

reactions.name: Net warm HCN/NH3 route to ornithine

conditions.other: Concentrated HCN/NH3 or NH4CN-rich warm pools; represented as a net route rather than a single elementary step

reactions.mechanism: HCN oligomerization or polymerization followed by aqueous breakdown releases trace diamino-acid products, represented here as a net formation of ornithine.
reactions.reasoning: Ruiz-Bermejo et al. (2013) summarize older hot HCN and NH4CN experiments in which ornithine was reported, and modern reanalysis of Miller samples independently confirms that ornithine can be formed abiotically in reduced-gas chemistry (Johnson et al., 2008; Parker et al., 2011). As a net HCN/NH3 route this remains low-confidence and probably low-yield, but it is more defensible than claiming direct arginine from HCN polymers.

reactions.name: Speculative cyanamide guanidinylation of ornithine

conditions.other: Concentrated prebiotic pools or mineral interfaces; prolonged residence or wet-dry concentration; alpha versus delta selectivity unresolved

reactions.mechanism: Terminal amine guanidinylation of ornithine by cyanamide gives arginine.
reactions.reasoning: Longo et al. (2020) demonstrated aqueous guanidination of ornithine side chains in a synthetic protein using a laboratory guanidinylating reagent and argued that cyanamide could serve as a primordial surrogate. However, no published prebiotic study has shown selective free ornithine plus cyanamide conversion to arginine in water, and Thoma and Powner (2023) highlight competing ornithine cyclization in related prebiotic chemistry. This route is chemically attractive as a late endgame but remains unverified for the free amino acid.

pathways.name: Endogenous cyanamide, aldehyde-first de novo cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: HCN and NH3 photochemistry supplies cyanamide in parallel with Cu(I)-mediated acrylonitrile formation; the C3 nitrile is reduced to the aldehyde, guanidinylated, homologated to arginine alpha-aminonitrile, and then hydrolyzed.

pathways.name: Environmental cyanamide, aldehyde-first de novo cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: As P1, but cyanamide is assumed to be already present in the pool, so the dedicated cyanamide-generation step is omitted.

pathways.name: Endogenous cyanamide, nitrile-first de novo cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: The C3 nitrile is guanidinylated before reduction; the guanidinylated nitrile is then speculatively reduced to the aldehyde analogue and carried through the Patel-like late homologation sequence.

pathways.name: Environmental cyanamide, nitrile-first de novo cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: As P3, but cyanamide is assumed to be exogenous rather than produced within the network.

pathways.name: Contested ornithine branch with endogenous cyanamide
pathways.description: Warm HCN and NH3 chemistry is treated as a net source of ornithine while parallel HCN photochemistry supplies cyanamide; late ornithine guanidinylation then gives arginine.

pathways.name: Contested ornithine branch with environmental cyanamide
pathways.description: As P5, but cyanamide is taken as externally available and only the ornithine-forming branch plus guanidinylation are required.

pathways.name: Acrylonitrile-entry aldehyde-first module
pathways.description: Starts from acrylonitrile rather than from its HCN and acetylene formation, then follows the reduction-first sequence to the target.

pathways.name: Acrylonitrile-entry nitrile-first module
pathways.description: Starts from acrylonitrile and follows nitrile-first guanidinylation, speculative reduction to the aldehyde analogue, and late homologation.

pathways.name: Late-stage aminoaldehyde module
pathways.description: Starts from beta-aminopropionaldehyde in a cyanamide-bearing pool and uses the experimentally motivated 37-type branch followed by late homologation and hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Late-stage guanidinylated nitrile module
pathways.description: Starts from the guanidinylated beta-aminopropionitrile 35-type intermediate and reaches arginine via speculative reduction to the aldehyde analogue, then Patel-like homologation and hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best endogenous de novo branch conceptually because it follows the literature-supported Patel aldehyde-first logic from acrylonitrile to intermediate 37 and then toward the arginine alpha-aminonitrile. The main problems are stoichiometric: rxn_001 is unbalanced and likely needs H2 as a coproduct, rxn_004 is not a valid H2S-only one-step conversion and likely omits H2O, NH3 and sulfur byproducts, rxn_008 collapses the documented multistep 37 -> 45 -> 46 chemistry into an unbalanced net that is short one carbon, and rxn_009 should include 2 H2O as reactants and NH3 as product. Literature alignment is good, but free arginine is not actually defended as formed here, and the final Biochemical step is not placed in a specific prebiotic setting.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_001 with explicit coproducts such as H2 or cite a balanced net photolysis of ammonium cyanide.
Split rxn_008 into the Patel-type intermediates 37 -> 45 -> 46 with explicit carbon sources and byproducts.
Write rxn_009 as aminonitrile hydrolysis with 2 H2O in and NH3 out, and justify mild prebiotic conditions that preserve the guanidino group.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest pathway in the network and the closest match to the Patel literature because it uses the experimentally favored aldehyde-first order. However, rxn_004, rxn_008 and rxn_009 are still unbalanced; rxn_008 in particular compresses several Patel steps and is short one carbon, while rxn_009 needs 2 H2O in and NH3 out. If cyanamide is intended to be environmental here, mol_004 should be declared as an explicit starting input or justified transfer. Surface chemistry is plausible up to the aminonitrile logic, but the final Biochemical hydrolysis is not a defended prebiotic environment.
suggestions: Declare environmental cyanamide as an explicit starting node or connect this route back to rxn_001.
Replace rxn_008 with the explicit multistep 37 -> 45 -> 46 sequence and correct the carbon count.
Specify a prebiotic hydrolysis setting for rxn_009 and include the missing 2 H2O and NH3.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The early steps to guanidinylated nitrile 35 are literature-supported, but Patel actually favors aldehyde-first capture because the 36 plus cyanamide reaction is efficient. This nitrile-first branch depends on rxn_007, an explicitly speculative and unbalanced 35-to-37 type reduction that likely omits H2O, NH3 and sulfur byproducts, then inherits the unbalanced compressed rxn_008 and the unbalanced hydrolysis rxn_009, which should include 2 H2O in and NH3 out. rxn_001 also needs H2 as coproduct if cyanamide is generated in-network.
suggestions: Prefer the aldehyde-first ordering unless experimental support for 35 to aldehyde conversion is added.
Remove or experimentally justify rxn_007 with explicit stoichiometry and products.
Repair rxn_001, rxn_008 and rxn_009 before treating this as a valid route to free arginine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Slightly cleaner than P3 only because it omits in-network cyanamide formation, but it remains substantially weaker than the aldehyde-first branch. rxn_007 is unbalanced and unsupported by the cited Patel chemistry, rxn_008 is an unbalanced one-step compression of a longer sequence and is short one carbon, and rxn_009 needs 2 H2O in and NH3 out. As written, this route is a speculative extrapolation rather than an experimentally grounded arginine pathway, and environmental cyanamide should be made explicit if that assumption is intended.
suggestions: Add mol_004 as a starting input if this is meant to be an environmental cyanamide variant.
Replace rxn_007 with experimentally supported chemistry or drop the nitrile-first branch.
Expand rxn_008 and correct rxn_009 stoichiometry before claiming free arginine production.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strategically honest about the ornithine endgame being contested, but chemically weak as encoded. rxn_010 is grossly unbalanced and does not represent any single literature route from HCN plus NH3 to ornithine; ornithine reports come from HCN-polymer hydrolysates or spark residues, not direct one-step conversion. rxn_011 is balanced and chemically conceivable, but free ornithine guanidinylation by cyanamide in water remains unverified, alpha versus delta selectivity is unresolved, and the Biochemical environment label is too vague to count as a defended prebiotic setting. rxn_001 also needs H2 as coproduct.
suggestions: Replace rxn_010 with an experimentally grounded multistep ornithine branch or remove the branch.
Provide evidence or justification for selective delta guanidinylation of free ornithine by cyanamide in water.
Define a real prebiotic aqueous environment for rxn_011 instead of using the generic Biochemical label.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the cleaner ornithine endgame because it avoids in-network cyanamide formation, but the core weakness remains. rxn_010 is still a severely unbalanced and under-specified stand-in for trace ornithine reports from very different chemistries, while rxn_011, although balanced, is not experimentally demonstrated for free ornithine under prebiotic aqueous conditions and has unresolved site selectivity. If cyanamide is environmental, that input should be explicit rather than implied.
suggestions: Make environmental cyanamide an explicit starting node for this pathway.
Do not encode HCN plus NH3 to ornithine as a one-step net reaction; replace it with a documented multistep or omit it.
Support rxn_011 with conditions and selectivity data, or keep this only as a speculative endgame.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: As a module, this tracks the strongest Patel ordering from acrylonitrile through the aminoaldehyde and cyanamide adduct. As a complete synthesis it is incomplete because acrylonitrile is taken as given, and rxn_004, rxn_008 and rxn_009 still suffer the same balance and endgame problems as P2: rxn_004 is not a valid H2S-only net, rxn_008 is an unbalanced compression of the late homologation sequence, and rxn_009 should include 2 H2O in and NH3 out.
suggestions: If this is intended as a full pathway, connect it upstream to rxn_002 or declare acrylonitrile as an input.
Expand rxn_008 into explicit late-stage intermediates instead of a one-step net.
Correct rxn_009 stoichiometry and specify mild prebiotic hydrolysis conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This module is weaker than P7 because it hinges on rxn_007, an unbalanced and explicitly speculative reduction from guanidinylated nitrile toward the aldehyde manifold that is not supported by Patel's reported sequence. Even before the final hydrolysis, rxn_008 remains an unbalanced one-step collapse of a longer late-stage homologation. The route is therefore only a tentative hypothesis around 35, not a validated module to arginine.
suggestions: Prefer the aldehyde-first module unless direct evidence for rxn_007 is added.
Connect the module upstream or clearly label it as a speculative late-stage test rather than a synthesis route.
Repair rxn_008 and rxn_009 stoichiometry before claiming target formation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Useful late-stage test module because the aminoaldehyde plus cyanamide step to intermediate 37 is experimentally strong. But the network still does not define a balanced route from 37 to the arginine aminonitrile: rxn_008 is unbalanced and missing at least one carbon equivalent, and rxn_009 remains an unbalanced and unverified hydrolysis to free arginine that should include 2 H2O in and NH3 out. So this is a plausible precursor module, not a demonstrated arginine module.
suggestions: Model the literature-supported late sequence explicitly rather than using a single rxn_008 net step.
Define the missing carbon source and byproducts in the conversion from 37 to the aminonitrile.
Correct rxn_009 stoichiometry and specify prebiotic hydrolysis conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This late-stage guanidinylated nitrile module is weak because it depends on rxn_007, an unbalanced and explicitly speculative 35-to-37 type reduction that is not supported by the cited Patel work. Even if that step were repaired, rxn_008 is still missing carbon and compresses a longer sequence, while rxn_009 is an unbalanced and unverified hydrolysis to free arginine. The module is therefore not chemically robust as written.
suggestions: Remove or experimentally support rxn_007 with explicit stoichiometry and identifiable byproducts.
Use the aminoaldehyde-first late-stage module instead if following the Patel literature.
Repair rxn_008 and rxn_009 before treating this as a target-achieving branch.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network topology is acceptable: 13 molecule nodes and 11 reaction nodes form a connected graph with consistent IDs. Literature alignment is better than the chemistry implementation: the strategy appropriately centers Patel-style cyanosulfidic chemistry, acknowledges that only the arginine alpha-aminonitrile is experimentally supported, treats ornithine guanidinylation as speculative, and does not rely on disputed direct-arginine claims. The limiting problem is validity and stoichiometry. RDKit finds 6 of 11 reactions unbalanced: rxn_001 likely needs H2 as coproduct; rxn_004 and rxn_007 cannot be represented as simple H2S-only reductions and likely omit H2O, NH3 and sulfur byproducts; rxn_008 is missing at least one carbon equivalent and compresses the 37 -> 45 -> 46 sequence into an unsupported one-step net; rxn_009 should include 2 H2O as reactants and NH3 as product; rxn_010 is grossly under-specified and not a credible single-step ornithine synthesis. rxn_011 is balanced but still unverified for free ornithine with cyanamide, and delta-selectivity is unresolved. Surface conditions are the best fit for the Patel-like chemistry, but the final Biochemical steps are not mapped onto defended prebiotic environments. Best branch is P2, but even that route only plausibly reaches the arginine alpha-aminonitrile logic, not defended free arginine. Not approved as submitted.
